25805-in-ancient-albemarle.title: Copyright, 1914
25805-in-ancient-albemarle.creator: Unknown
25805-in-ancient-albemarle.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Thus, half asleep, I dream along,  Till low at first, and far away,  Then louder, more insistent, calls  A voice my heart would fain obey. And by a force resistless drawn,  The narrow banks that fetter me  I thrust apart, and onward sweep  In quiet strength toward the sea.

66831-modern-essays-and-stories-a-book-t.title: For Writing, And Original Illustrations
66831-modern-essays-and-stories-a-book-t.creator: Unknown
66831-modern-essays-and-stories-a-book-t.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Then again, who would wish to learn to write like Addison, like Washington Irving, like Macaulay, or like Carlyle! Those great writers couched their thoughts in the language-fashions of their days, just as they clothed their bodies in the garments of their times. To imitate either their style of expression or their costumes would be to make one's self ridiculous, or to take part in a species of masquerade.

Li’s research
arxiv-1511-06902.creator: Yun Shen Lihua You Minjie Zhang Shuchao Li
arxiv-1511-06902.description: Abstract Abstract A connected graph G is a cactus if any two of its cycles have at most one common vertex. Let \ell_{n}^{m} be the set of cacti on n vertices with matching number m. S.C. Li and M.J. Zhang determined the unique graph with the maximum signless Laplacian spectral radius among all cacti in \ell_{n}^{m} with n=2m .

arxiv-1805-11434.title: Spectrum management and compatibility studies with Python
arxiv-1805-11434.description: Abstract We developed the pycraf Python package, which provides functions and procedures for various tasks related to spectrum-management compatibility studies. This includes an implementation of 11 , which allows to calculate the path attenuation arising from the distance and terrain properties between an interferer and the victim service.

arxiv-2203-05386.title: Faking Fake News for Real Fake News Detection: Propaganda-loaded Training Data Generation
arxiv-2203-05386.creator: Kung-Hsiang Huang Kathleen McKeown, Preslav Nakov Yejin Choi Heng Ji
arxiv-2203-05386.description: Abstract Despite recent advances in detecting fake news generated by neural models, their results are not readily applicable to effective detection of human-written disinformation. What limits the successful transfer between them is the sizable gap between machine-generated fake news and human-authored ones, including the notable differences in terms of style and underlying intent.

arxiv-2211-08186.title: A Roadmap to Decipher Ultrafast Photophysics in Two-Dimensional Nanomaterials
arxiv-2211-08186.creator: Pieter Schiettecatte, Zeger Hens, Pieter Geiregat
arxiv-2211-08186.description: Abstract Atomically thin two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors are extensively investigated for opto-electronic applications that require strong light-matter interactions. In view of such applications, it is essential to understand how (photo)excitation alters the non-linear optical response of these materials under high carrier density conditions.

arxiv-2305-12868.title: NAS-FM: Neural Architecture Search for Tunable and Interpretable Sound Synthesis based on Frequency Modulation
arxiv-2305-12868.creator: Zhen Ye, Wei Xue ∗, Xu Tan, Qifeng Liu, Yike Guo
arxiv-2305-12868.description: Abstract Developing digital sound synthesizers is crucial to the music industry as it provides a low-cost way to produce high-quality sounds with rich timbres. Existing traditional synthesizers often require substantial expertise to determine the overall framework of a synthesizer and the parameters of submodules.

arxiv-2306-16283.title: Schwinger poles of the three-gluon vertex: symmetry and dynamics
arxiv-2306-16283.creator: A. C. Aguilar, M. N. Ferreira, B. M. Oliveira, J. Papavassiliou, L. R. Santos
arxiv-2306-16283.description: Abstract The implementation of the Schwinger mechanism endows gluons with a nonperturbative mass through the formation of special massless poles in the fundamental QCD vertices; due to their longitudinal character, these poles do not cause divergences in on-shell amplitudes, but induce detectable effects in the Green’s functions of the theory.

arxiv-2307-03176.title: Learning Curves for Noisy Heterogeneous Feature-Subsampled Ridge Ensembles
arxiv-2307-03176.creator: Benjamin S. Ruben 1 , Cengiz Pehlevan 2,3,4 1 Biophysics Graduate Program 2 Center for Brain Science, 3 John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences, 4 Kempner Institute for the Study of Natural and Artificial Intelligence, Harvard University Cambridge, MA 02138 benruben@g.harvard.edu
arxiv-2307-03176.description: Abstract Feature bagging is a well-established ensembling method which aims to reduce prediction variance by combining predictions of many estimators trained on subsets or projections of features. Here, we develop a theory of feature-bagging in noisy least-squares ridge ensembles and simplify the resulting learning curves in the special case of equicorrelated data.

arxiv-2309-02076.title: MeerKAT HI-line observations of the nearby interacting galaxy pair NGC 1512/1510 MeerKAT HI-line observations of the nearby interacting galaxy pair NGC 1512/1510 – References

arxiv-2309-02076.description: Abstract We present MeerKAT H i line observations of the nearby interacting galaxy pair NGC 1512/1510. The MeerKAT data yield high-fidelity image sets characterised by an excellent combination of high angular resolution ( ∼ 20 ′′ \sim 20^{\prime\prime} ) and and sensitivity ( ∼ 0.08 \sim 0.

arxiv-2407-18320.title: Solving physics-based initial value problems with unsupervised machine learning
arxiv-2407-18320.creator: Jack Griffiths, Steven A. Wrathmall, Simon A. Gardiner
arxiv-2407-18320.description: Abstract Initial value problems — a system of ordinary differential equations and corresponding initial conditions — can be used to describe many physical phenomena including those arise in classical mechanics. We have developed a novel approach to solve physics-based initial value problems using unsupervised machine learning.

arxiv-2410-08570.title: Predictive Tree-based Virtual Keyboard for Improved Gaze Typing
arxiv-2410-08570.creator: Hrushikesh Etikikota, Yogesh Kumar Meena
arxiv-2410-08570.description: Abstract On-screen keyboard eye-typing systems are limited due to the lack of predictive text and user-centred approaches, resulting in low text entry rates and frequent recalibration. This work proposes integrating the prediction by partial matching (PPM) technique into a tree-based virtual keyboard.

arxiv-2410-23797.title: Gardner transition coincides with the emergence of jamming scalings in hard spheres and disks
arxiv-2410-23797.creator: Qi Wang, Deng Pan, Yuliang Jin
arxiv-2410-23797.description: Abstract The Gardner transition in structural glasses is characterized by full-replica symmetry breaking of the free-energy landscape and the onset of anomalous aging dynamics due to marginal stability. Here we show that this transition also has a structural signature in finite-dimensional glasses consisting of hard spheres and disks.

arxiv-2501-14851.title: JustLogic: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Deductive Reasoning in Large Language Models
arxiv-2501-14851.creator: Michael K. Chen, Xikun Zhang, Dacheng Tao
arxiv-2501-14851.description: Abstract Logical reasoning is a critical component of Large Language Models (LLMs), and substantial research efforts in recent years have aimed to enhance their deductive reasoning capabilities. However, existing deductive reasoning benchmarks, which are crucial for evaluating and advancing LLMs, are inadequate due to their lack of task complexity, presence of prior knowledge as a confounder, and superficial error analysis.

arxiv-2503-23600.title: Online Convex Optimization and Integral Quadratic Constraints: An automated approach to regret analysis
arxiv-2503-23600.creator: Fabian Jakob, Andrea Iannelli
arxiv-2503-23600.description: Abstract We propose a novel approach for analyzing dynamic regret of first-order online convex optimization (OCO) algorithms for strongly convex and Lipschitz-smooth objectives. Crucially, we provide a general analysis that is applicable to a wide range of first-order algorithms that can be expressed as an interconnection of a linear dynamical system in feedback with a first-order oracle.

pmc-10525261.title: Role of Cardio-Renal Dysfunction, Inflammation Markers, and Frailty on In-Hospital Mortality in Older COVID-19 Patients: A Cluster Analysis
pmc-10525261.creator: Francesco Spannella, Federico Giulietti, Giorgia Laureti, Mirko Di Rosa, Chiara Di Pentima, Massimiliano Allevi, Caterina Garbuglia, Piero Giordano, Matteo Landolfo, Letizia Ferrara, Alessia Fumagalli, Fabrizia Lattanzio, Anna Rita Bonfigli, Riccardo Sarzani
pmc-10525261.description: Our study aimed to identify clusters of hospitalized older COVID-19 patients according to their main comorbidities and routine laboratory parameters to evaluate their association with in-hospital mortality. We performed an observational study on 485 hospitalized older COVID-19 adults (aged 80+ years). Patients were aggregated in clusters by a K-medians cluster analysis. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality.

pmc-11569325.title: Essential Reads in Rhinology: A Bibliometric Analysis
pmc-11569325.creator: Ariana L Shaari, Shreya Bhalla, Rebecca Ho, Anup Dupaguntla, Sylvia Zabielski, Wayne Hsueh, Jean Anderson Eloy, Andrey Filimonov
pmc-11569325.description: AimsRhinology is a progressive subspecialty within otolaryngology. Bibliometric analysis is a powerful method to survey the landscape of literature on a specific topic and identify publication trends. We aimed to analyze the 50 most impactful English-language rhinology manuscripts of all time to create a targeted reading list for otolaryngologists.

pmc-11665180.title: How Can Outdoor Air Pollutants Adversely Affect the Women's Fertility? Systematic Review
pmc-11665180.creator: Masoomeh Latifi, Forough Rahim, Mojtaba Ahmadlou, Nima Pouladian, Leili Allahbakhshian
pmc-11665180.description: In the current century, air pollution is known as one of the most critical environmental problems and it is important to find the relations of air pollution and human health. Various air pollutants, such as volatile organic compounds (VOCs), can negatively affect women's fertility.

pmc-12385384.description: BackgroundStudies on the impact and attention of cover papers within open-access journals from the same publisher remain lacking. pmc-12503296.title: Detection, transport, and retention of Toxoplasma gondii oocysts in saturated sandy porous media: Influence of electrolytes and natural organic matter in flow-through systems
pmc-12503296.creator: Christian P. Pullano, Mahsa Ghorbani, Timothy J. Mutty, Sohib Gouasmia, Coralie L’Ollivier, Jitender P. Dubey, Aurélien Dumètre, Christophe J. G. Darnault
pmc-12503296.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Understanding the transport and retention of Toxoplasma gondii oocysts through soils and into ground and surface water is essential for determining the risk this parasite poses to water resources and human health worldwide.

pmc-12562330.title: Upper Cervical Manipulation and Manual Massage Do Not Modulate Sympatho-Vagal Balance or Blood Pressure in Women: A Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trial
pmc-12562330.creator: Estêvão Rios Monteiro, Linda S Pescatello, Gustavo Henrique Garcia, Alexandre Gonçalves de Meirelles, Francine de Oliveira, Rafael Cotta de Souza, Leandro Alberto Calazans Nogueira, Agnaldo José Lopes, Daniel Moreira-Gonçalves
pmc-12562330.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Objectives: To compare the acute effects of upper cervical manipulation (CM) and manual massage (MM) to simulated CM (Sham) and Control conditions (Control) on heart rate variability (HRV) and blood pressure (BP) responses in women with non-elevated BP. Methods: A single-blind, four-arm, parallel-group, randomized, crossover, placebo-controlled trial recruited 15 apparently healthy women with non-elevated BP who visited the lab on four occasions with 48 h intervals to ensure adequate washout between interventions.

pmc-12662168.title: Evolution of floral traits and mating systems under drought: a range-wide study of Mimulus cardinalis
pmc-12662168.creator: Olivia Wilborn-Pilotte, Emily Cook, Katelin Kutella, Seema Nayan Sheth, Jeff Diez, F Xavier Picó, Christopher G Oakley
pmc-12662168.description: Climate change is intensifying droughts across the globe, challenging species to adapt to novel conditions. While plant physiological and phenological responses to drought are well-documented, less is known about how water scarcity affects the evolution of selfing across species ranges.

pmc-12717233.title: Belief embodiment through eye movements facilitates memory-guided navigation
pmc-12717233.creator: Akis Stavropoulos, Kaushik J Lakshminarasimhan, Dora E Angelaki
pmc-12717233.description: The brain evolved to navigate a dynamic and uncertain world, but the mechanisms underlying ethologically-relevant behavioral strategies remain unclear. In the real-world, such strategies are shaped both by task demands and by the cognitive resources available to the animal. We hypothesized that eye movements constitute a vital cognitive resource to support neural computations for memory-guided navigation.

pmc-13401605.title: Prediction of single cell expression from low-plex immunofluorescence images for guiding precision oncology

pmc-13593748.title: Why we believe chatbots: trust calibration as a design problem
pmc-13593748.creator: Kokil Jaidka, Mengxuan Cai
pmc-13593748.description: Chatbots powered by large language models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT and Claude, answer questions quickly and fluently, yet they reveal little about how their answers are produced or what evidence supports them. Users tend to trust these systems based on surface qualities such as fluency, confidence, and speed.

pmc-13639675.title: Clinical outcomes of radiation therapy as an alternative to radical surgery for early-stage rectal cancer
pmc-13639675.creator: Seo Jin Lee, Hwa Kyung Byun, Jee Suk Chang, Seo Hee Choi, Woo Joong Rhee, Jae Young Lee, Woong Sub Koom
pmc-13639675.description: PurposeTotal mesorectal excision (TME) is the standard treatment for early rectal cancer, but radiation therapy (RT) with or without chemotherapy may be considered as an alternative organ-preserving option. This study evaluated the oncologic outcomes, patterns of failure, salvage treatment efficacy, and TME–free survival (TME-FS) following RT without radical surgery after local excision or biopsy in selected patients.
